units.text: 1. An initiative project may be submitted to the Administration of the City of Yekaterinburg to implement measures of priority importance to residents of the municipality or part of it, addressing matters of local significance or other matters that the municipality’s local self-government bodies have been granted the right to address.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 17

units.text: 2. The initiative to submit an initiative project may be put forward by an initiative group of at least ten citizens who have reached sixteen years of age and reside in the municipality, territorial public self-government bodies, or the headperson of a rural settlement. The minimum size of the initiative group may be reduced by a decision of the City Duma. A decision of the City Duma may also grant other persons carrying out activities in the municipality’s territory the right to initiate a project.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 17

units.text: 3. An initiative project must meet the requirements established by Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’.
units.label: Point 3 Art. 17

units.text: 4. The procedure for proposing, submitting, discussing and considering initiative projects and conducting their competitive selection is established by the City Duma.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 17

units.text: 5. Other matters concerning the proposing, submission, discussion and consideration of initiative projects, their competitive selection, and financial and other support for their implementation are regulated in accordance with the requirements established by Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 17

units.text: Article 18. Territorial public self-government
units.label: Art. 18

units.text: 1. The population of the municipality has the right to organize itself at its place of residence in part of the municipality’s territory (an entrance section of an apartment building, an apartment building, a group of residential buildings, a residential microdistrict, settlements and other populated places within the municipality, or other areas where citizens reside) to implement its own initiatives on matters of local significance independently and under its own responsibility.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 18

units.text: The boundaries of the territory in which territorial public self-government is exercised are established by the City Duma on the proposal of the population residing in that territory.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 18 · “The boundaries of the territory in which territorial public…”

units.text: 2. Territorial public self-government is exercised through citizens’ meetings and conferences and through the establishment of territorial public self-government bodies elected at meetings and conferences of citizens residing in the relevant territory.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 18

units.text: 3. Territorial public self-government may, in accordance with its charter, constitute a legal entity and is subject to state registration in the organizational and legal form of a non-profit organization. Territorial public self-government is deemed established upon registration of its charter.
units.label: Point 3 Art. 18

units.text: 4. The procedure for registering the charter of territorial public self-government is determined by a decision of the City Duma.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 18

units.text: 5. The procedure for organizing and exercising territorial public self-government and the conditions and procedure for allocating the necessary funds from the municipal budget are determined by decisions of the City Duma.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 18

units.text: Article 18-1. Headperson of a rural settlement
units.label: Point 5 Art. 18 · “Article 18-1. Headperson of a rural settlement”

units.text: 1. To organize interaction between the municipality’s local self-government bodies and residents of a rural settlement in addressing matters of local significance, a headperson may be appointed in a rural settlement situated within the municipality.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 18

units.text: 2. The headperson of a rural settlement is appointed by the City Duma on the nomination of the settlement’s citizens’ assembly. The headperson is appointed from among citizens of the Russian Federation residing in that rural settlement and entitled to vote, or citizens of the Russian Federation who have reached 18 years of age on the date of nomination by the citizens’ assembly and own residential premises situated in that rural settlement.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 18

units.text: 3. The headperson of a rural settlement is not a person holding a state office, a state civil service position, a municipal office other than the municipal office of a City Duma deputy exercising powers on a non-permanent basis, or a municipal service position, and may not have employment relations or other relations directly connected with them with local self-government bodies.
units.label: Point 3 Art. 18

units.text: 4. A person may not be appointed headperson of a rural settlement in the cases established by Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 18

units.text: 5. The term of office of the headperson of a rural settlement is two years.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 18

units.text: The powers of the headperson of a rural settlement terminate early by decision of the City Duma on the proposal of the settlement’s citizens’ assembly, and in the cases established by Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 18 · “The powers of the headperson of a rural settlement terminate…”

units.text: 6. To perform the tasks assigned to them, the headperson of a rural settlement:
units.label: Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 1) interacts with the municipality’s local self-government bodies, municipal enterprises and institutions, and other organizations on addressing matters of local significance in the rural settlement;
units.label: Subpoint 1 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 2) interacts with the population, including through participation in citizens’ assemblies, meetings and conferences, and, following those events, submits appeals and proposals, including in the form of draft municipal legal acts, which must be considered by the municipality’s local self-government bodies;
units.label: Subpoint 2 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 3) informs residents of the rural settlement about the organization and exercise of local self-government and assists in communicating to them other information received from the municipality’s local self-government bodies;
units.label: Subpoint 3 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 4) assists the municipality’s local self-government bodies in organizing and conducting public hearings and public discussions and promulgating their results in the rural settlement;
units.label: Subpoint 4 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 5) may initiate submission of an initiative project on matters of priority importance to residents of the rural settlement;
units.label: Subpoint 5 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 6) exercises other powers and rights provided for by a decision of the City Duma in accordance with a law of Sverdlovsk Oblast.
units.label: Subpoint 6 Point 6 Art. 18

units.text: 7. Guarantees for the activities of a rural settlement’s headperson and other matters concerning their status may be established by a decision of the City Duma in accordance with a law of Sverdlovsk Oblast.
units.label: Point 7 Art. 18

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.label: Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 1. The Head of Yekaterinburg and the City Duma may hold public hearings to discuss draft municipal legal acts on matters of local significance with the participation of residents of the municipality.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 2. Public hearings are held on the initiative of the population, the City Duma or the Head of Yekaterinburg.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: Public hearings held on the initiative of the population or the City Duma are called by the City Duma; those held on the initiative of the Head of Yekaterinburg are called by the Head of Yekaterinburg.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 19 · “Public hearings held on the initiative of the population or the…”

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 3. The following must be submitted to public hearings:
units.label: Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 1) the draft Charter of the Municipality “City of Yekaterinburg” and a draft decision of the City Duma amending or supplementing that Charter, except where amendments exactly reproduce provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, or the Charter or laws of Sverdlovsk Oblast in order to bring the Charter of the Municipality “City of Yekaterinburg” into conformity with those regulatory legal acts;
units.label: Subpoint 1 Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 2) the draft municipal budget and the report on its execution;
units.label: Subpoint 2 Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 3) the draft socioeconomic development strategy of the municipality;
units.label: Subpoint 3 Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 4) matters concerning transformation of the municipality, except where Article 13 of Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’ requires the population’s consent to the transformation to be obtained through a vote;
units.label: Subpoint 4 Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 5) repealed by Decision of the Yekaterinburg City Duma of 10.04.2018 No. 9/78.
units.label: Subpoint 5 Point 3 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 4. The procedure for organizing and holding public hearings is determined by a decision of the City Duma.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 5. The results of public hearings, including the reasoned justification for decisions adopted, are subject to publication (promulgation).
units.label: Point 5 Art. 19

units.locator: Article 19. Public hearings and public discussions
units.text: 6. Public hearings or public discussions are held, in accordance with urban planning legislation, on draft master plans; draft land use and development rules; draft territorial planning and land subdivision plans; draft territorial improvement rules; drafts amending any of those approved documents; draft decisions granting permission for a conditionally permitted use of a land plot or capital construction facility; draft decisions granting permission to depart from the limiting parameters of permitted construction or reconstruction of capital construction facilities; and changes from one permitted use of land plots or capital construction facilities to another where no approved land use and development rules exist.
units.label: Point 6 Art. 19

units.text: Article 20. Citizens’ meeting
units.label: Art. 20

units.text: 1. Citizens’ meetings may be held to discuss matters of local significance, inform the population of the municipality about the activities of local self-government bodies and officials, discuss the submission and consideration of initiative projects, and exercise territorial public self-government in part of the municipality’s territory.
units.label: Point 1 Art. 20

units.text: 2. Citizens’ meetings are held on the basis of and in accordance with Federal Law of 6 October 2003 No. 131-ФЗ ‘On the General Principles of the Organization of Local Self-Government in the Russian Federation’ and this Charter.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 20

units.text: 3. A citizens’ meeting is held on the initiative of the municipality’s population, the City Duma or the Head of Yekaterinburg, and in cases provided for by the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Point 3 Art. 20

units.text: 4. A citizens’ meeting held on the initiative of the City Duma or the Head of Yekaterinburg is called, respectively, by the City Duma or the Head of Yekaterinburg in accordance with the procedure established by the City Duma.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 20

units.text: A citizens’ meeting held on the initiative of the municipality’s population is called by the City Duma in accordance with the procedure established by this Charter.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 20 · “A citizens’ meeting held on the initiative of the…”

units.text: The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting to exercise territorial public self-government is determined by the charter of territorial public self-government.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 20 · “The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting to…”

units.text: The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting to consider and discuss the submission of initiative projects is determined by a decision of the City Duma. Residents of the relevant territory who have reached sixteen years of age may participate in a citizens’ meeting on the submission and consideration of initiative projects.
units.label: Point 4 Art. 20 · “The procedure for calling and holding a citizens’ meeting to…”

units.text: 5. When citizens’ meetings are held on the initiative of the municipality’s population, they are organized by an initiative group of at least ten citizens residing in the relevant territory.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20

units.text: The citizens’ initiative group decides to hold a citizens’ meeting and submits an appeal to the City Duma proposing that the meeting be called, which must state:
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “The citizens’ initiative group decides to hold a citizens’…”

units.text: the place and time of the meeting;
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “the place and time of the meeting;”

units.text: the matters to be submitted for discussion at the citizens’ meeting;
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “the matters to be submitted for discussion at the citizens’…”

units.text: the reasons why those matters need to be discussed at the meeting;
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “the reasons why those matters need to be discussed at the…”

units.text: the territory within which the citizens’ meeting is proposed to be held;
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “the territory within which the citizens’ meeting is proposed to…”

units.text: the list of citizens’ initiative group members, stating each member’s surname, given name, patronymic, place of residence and contact telephone numbers.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “the list of citizens’ initiative group members, stating each…”

units.text: The appeal must be signed by all members of the initiative group.
units.label: Point 5 Art. 20 · “The appeal must be signed by all members of the initiative…”

units.text: 6. Within no more than one month after receiving the initiative group’s appeal, the City Duma decides to call the citizens’ meeting or to refuse to call it, and informs the initiative group of its decision in writing.
units.label: Point 6 Art. 20

units.text: 7. A citizens’ meeting may be refused only where the initiative group has breached point 5 of this Article.
units.label: Point 7 Art. 20

units.text: 8. The City Duma’s decision calling a citizens’ meeting on the initiative of the municipality’s population specifies the place and time of the meeting and the matters to be discussed.
units.label: Point 8 Art. 20

units.text: 9. The City Duma’s decision or the Head of Yekaterinburg’s resolution calling a citizens’ meeting on the initiative of those local self-government bodies specifies the place and time of the meeting, the matters to be discussed, and the local self-government officials responsible for preparing the meeting.
units.label: Point 9 Art. 20

units.text: The Head of Yekaterinburg approves plans of organizational measures for convening citizens’ meetings and prepares the documents and materials necessary for holding them.
units.label: Point 9 Art. 20 · “The Head of Yekaterinburg approves plans of organizational…”

units.text: 10. The decision to hold a citizens’ meeting and the documents and materials submitted to it are communicated to the municipality’s population through the mass media or by other means in advance, but no later than three days before the meeting.
units.label: Point 10 Art. 20

units.text: 11. The Head of Yekaterinburg and other local self-government officials of the municipality assist citizens in obtaining premises for a citizens’ meeting within their respective powers.
units.label: Point 11 Art. 20

units.text: 12. The powers of a citizens’ meeting include the right to consider and decide any matters significant to its territory, except matters within the powers of the municipality’s local self-government bodies, officials of state authorities and local self-government bodies, organizations of various forms of ownership, or public associations.
units.label: Point 12 Art. 20
